eval.title: Adobe ADBE Stock - Time To Power Up Excel!!!

call.headline_quote: Therefore, on our quadrant, I put and I'll keep Adobe on a bet because it's too much of a bet for me.

base_metric.name: eps
base_metric.quote: Let's start with the normal case scenario, 17 earnings per share, the GAAP earnings, not the non-GAAP crazy earnings.

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: Growth rate, if I estimate those earnings growing 8% over the next 5 years, 6% over the subsequent 5 years, I expect a 10% return, that's a discount rate of 10%. If I put a P/E ratio of 15, that's the intrinsic value, close to the stock price.

scenarios.name: best
scenarios.quote: If we go to the best-case scenario, if we put 13% 12% growth rates, terminal multiple of 20 P ratio of 20, Adobe stock would need to double double just to give you a 10% return, which means that the true return is much higher.

scenarios.name: worst
scenarios.quote: Let's say 4% growth, then 4% decline, discount rate 10%, P ratio where it is now of 10 down the road. Terminal value in 10 years, 175, so you lose money down the road.

reasons.claim: Revenue and earnings growth are decelerating and Wall Street is scared by this trend.
reasons.quote: The key factor is the deceleration is ongoing and that scares Wall Street.

reasons.claim: Adobe is growing slower than the highly competitive market, meaning it is losing market share.
reasons.quote: It's growing, but Adobe is growing slower, which means it's losing market share.

reasons.claim: Reported stock-based compensation understates the true dilution cost, which cancels out most of the buyback benefit.
reasons.quote: Adobe spending around 2 billion annually for stock-based compensation. And then, if we dig deeper, the dilution rate is 3% annually.

data_check.gap_note: he says 2, as-of 195.16 (2026-06-18); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: A recession scenario, unseen for 17 years, could collapse earnings and send the stock 40% lower.
reasons.quote: Earnings collapse, go from 17 to 10. P/E ratio of 12. The stock price is 120, which is another, what is it, 40% down from here.

data_check.gap_note: he says 10, as-of 16.7 (FY2025); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: recession-case pe, downside

reasons.claim: Leadership turnover (CEO then CFO departures) adds uncertainty at a time the business is already decelerating.
reasons.quote: They have lost the CEO, now the CFO, and things are changing a little bit. This is a question mark, but if it is a good business, then this shouldn't be an issue.

external_facts_used: Michael Burry's Adobe full position and his seven-position portfolio strategy
Adobe's shift from user growth metrics to annualized recurring revenue disclosure, interpreted as a sign of pricing pressure
